feedback.problem: Find all of the solutions to ${x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+9x-9=0$ given that $x=-3\text{i}$ is a solution.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x)={x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+9x-9.$ 

Since $f(x)$ has real coefficients and ${x}_{1}=-3\text{i}$ is a root of $f(x),$ the complex conjugate 

$$
\overset{―}{{x}_{1}}=\overset{―}{-3\text{i}}=3\text{i}
$$

must also be a root of $f(x).$

Now, according to the factor theorem, 
$(x-3\text{i})(x-(-3\text{i}))$
is a factor of $f(x).$ Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3\text{i})(x-(-3\text{i})) & ={x}^{2}+(3\text{i})(-3\text{i}) \\  & ={x}^{2}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+9$ using polynomial division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\,x-1\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \\  & {x}^{2}+9\,\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+9x-9\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{3}+9x}_{―} \\  & -{x}^{2}\,\,-9 \\  & \,{-\,{x}^{2}\,\,-9}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

  

Thus, $f(x)=({x}^{2}+9)(x-1).$ 

To find the remaining root, we set the linear factor equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1=0\,⟹\,x=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the roots are $x=1,\pm 3\text{i}.$
